summary:
The scouting hypotheses hold, and I measured them. Every longitudinal curve the loft samples is piecewise linear (np.interp). Two of them have real defects: the deck outline steps by +9.5 mm at x=7300, and bottom_z steps by 91 mm at x=1008. The 5-point moving-average fairing (_fair) adds an S-bend at the bow and pulls the curves 6-13 mm away from the measured data. The loft only sees these curves at 42 cosine-spaced stations (4, 13, 51, ..., 7153, 7335, ..., 7948). The exact B-rep deck edge (I built the loft from a scratch copy of the repo) is smooth amidships: short-wave wiggle is only 0.30 mm full scale over x=1500-6800. The topside waterlines are wavy, though: 11-18 curvature sign changes each, with the peaks sitting 0-7 mm from the stations. That comes from the kinked WATERPLANE and SECTION_FULLNESS tables.

The biggest robot effect on the deck line is in the STL, not the CAD. build.py:221 exports with CadQuery's default relative=True deflection, so the 263 mm long deck-edge edge gets an allowed sag of about 2.4 model mm. In 01_skrog.stl that edge is only 17 vertices from x=333 to 7701: 16 straight segments 336-768 mm long, with a 1.0-3.35 deg corner at each vertex in plan and up to 2.5 deg in profile. The STL deck edge's short-wave wiggle is 2.59 mm. That is 8.6x the B-rep, and more than the Bambu max-beam line (1.76 mm, which is itself less fair than our CAD).

The deck and sheer can be faired without losing accuracy. A least-squares spline for the deck outline (max residual 10.9-11.2 mm, within the 12.5 mm line width of the 1:50 drawing; the current curve is off by up to 13.5 mm) and a smoothing spline for the sheer (max 5.0 mm, versus 7.1 mm today) remove the kinks and the step. They also bring the curves closer to the measured points than today.

Correction to the task brief: 01_skrog.stl is rotated +45 deg, not +44. At -45.00 the hull midline is symmetric to 0.01 model mm; at -44 it is off by 1.33 mm, and every plan comparison done at 44 is skewed by up to 60 mm full scale at the ends. Also note: hull_stations.csv's 'faired' deck column is the raw trace resampled to a 150 mm grid (they agree within 3 mm everywhere), so no fairing had been done before _fair.

Images: 1 = curvature of every curve as used, plus the exact-loft lines with station positions marked. 2 = the STL deck edge as a staircase against the function, the loft and Bambu. 3 = before/after fairing for the sheer and deck outline, with the deviation from the measured points.

Scripts and data are in the scratch folder C:/Users/stig/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/12681ed4fad82730/bbd7b4f2-5285-465a-8464-b20ca4b41c67/scratchpad/robot/curves (a1_curves.py, a3_loft.py, a4_lines.py, a6_analyze.py, a7_fair_plot.py; the Bambu scripts run with python -I). Nothing in the repo was touched.

findings.title: STL turns the deck edge (and every long edge) into a 16-segment polyline: relative tessellation
findings.claim: The smooth B-rep deck edge reaches 01_skrog.stl as 17 vertices and 16 straight segments between x=333 and 7701. CadQuery exports with relative=True by default, so the 0.018 tolerance is multiplied by the edge size and only the 0.12 rad angle limit applies.
findings.evidence:
hr26/build.py:221 calls cq.exporters.export(wp, fn, tolerance=0.018, angularTolerance=0.12). That reaches cadquery/occ_impl/exporters/__init__.py:129 (shape.exportStl(fname, tolerance, angularTolerance, useascii)). Shape.exportStl has relative=True as its default (occ_impl/shapes.py:490). For the 263 mm (model) deck-edge edge OCCT then allows a sag of about 0.5 x 263 x 0.018 = 2.4 model mm (about 71 mm full scale).

Measured on the starboard deck-edge crease of the STL (un-rotated by -45 deg):
- Vertices: x = 333, 803, 1571, 2034, 2452, 3162, 3566, 4061, 4521, 4857, 5204, 5550, 5896, 6356, 6872, 7325, 7701.
- Segments are 336-768 mm long (11-26 mm in the model).
- Plan corners at each vertex: 1.9, 1.2, 2.0, 1.6, 2.2, 3.35, 3.1, 3.3, 3.2, 3.2, 2.5, 1.9, 2.3, 2.5, 1.0 deg. Profile corners up to 2.5 deg at 6872 and 7325.
- Chord sag against the true curve: 1.6-6.9 mm full in plan (0.05-0.23 model mm; largest in segment 6872-7325), and up to 3.0 mm in profile.
- Short-wave (<1 m) deviation: STL deck edge max 2.59 mm (rms 0.83), exact B-rep deck edge 0.30 mm, Bambu max-beam line 1.76 mm.

Image 2 shows the heading of the line as a staircase.
findings.where: hr26/build.py:221 (export); affects every long B-rep edge and face of 01_skrog.stl
findings.fix: Export the hull with an absolute deflection, for example wp.val().exportStl(fn, tolerance=0.01, angularTolerance=0.05, relative=False). That gives about 0.3 mm full scale, and the deck-edge segments would drop to roughly 25-35 mm full. cq.exporters.export cannot pass relative=False, so call Shape.exportStl directly.
findings.risk: The STL gets 3-10x more triangles and slices more slowly; there is no geometric risk. Check the file size against what Bambu Studio handles.

findings.title: deck_half_breadth steps +9.5 mm at x=7300 (faired table to raw STERN_OUTLINE)
findings.claim: The deck outline is not even C0. Below 7300 it comes from the faired table (985.5 mm at 7300); from 7300 it comes from the raw STERN_OUTLINE (995.0). The fairing ran on a table into which the stern values had already been substituted, and it pulled them down (969.2 at 7350, against 981.5 in the outline).
findings.evidence:
curves.py:54 substitutes STERN_OUTLINE before _fair; curves.py:70 fairs it; curves.py:83-85 switches at _SX[0]=7300.

Kink table for deck_half_breadth as used (x<7300 from _HB, then STERN_OUTLINE): -2.1 deg at 7300, +1.6 at 7400 and -2.1 at 7500, so the curvature reverses sign there.

In the exact loft (scratch rebuild, 42 stations) the deck edge bulges +8.2 mm from the function at x=7225-7295, between stations 7153 and 7335, and its plan curvature changes sign at 7135 and 7185.

The same hb feeds deck_camber, the cockpit width (hb-290) and the coaming width (hb-200).
findings.fix: Fit one continuous spline through the trace (x<7300) and STERN_OUTLINE together (see curves-9), and stop switching sources at 7300.
findings.risk: Low. It changes the stern deck width at 7200-7400 by at most about 10 mm toward the measured outline.

findings.title: _fair end effect: bow S-bend in the deck line and strake, and the sheer pulled 6-7 mm off the measured table
findings.claim: _fair (a 5-point moving average, 2 passes) leaves the first and last two samples untouched and averages the third over 0-600 mm. At the bow the deck half-breadth at x=300 drops 11 mm (222.6, against 233.6 in the CSV and 234.5 in the raw trace), which creates an S-bend. The cosine station spacing is densest exactly there, so the loft reproduces it. The same averaging cuts the measured curvature of the sheer.
findings.evidence:
curves.py:60-66, 69-73.

Kinks in deck_half_breadth: -11.4 deg at x=150, +3.9 deg at 300, -2.2 deg at 450.

The exact B-rep deck edge follows it through stations 4, 13, 51, 116, 205, 318, 455, 615 and 797. Its plan curvature swings +0.75, -1.6, +0.9, -0.55, +0.15 1/m between x of about 60 and 620 (Image 1, top).

strake_z shows the same effect: -0.70 deg at 150 and +0.35 deg at 300.

sheer_z minus DECK_EDGE_Z: -5.8 mm at 2000, -3.8 at 6500, -7.0 at 7000, -6.5 at 7200, -7.1 at 7400.

The current deck curve is also 8.3 mm narrower than the trace at maximum beam (1340.4 against 1348.7 at x=4931).
findings.where: hr26/curves.py:60-73 (_fair, passes); used by deck_half_breadth (85), sheer_z (101), strake_z (106), bottom_z (119)
findings.fix: Drop _fair for hb, zs and zk and use the fairing splines from curves-9. If a moving average is kept, pad the ends by reflection first (np.pad(y, h, mode='reflect', reflect_type='odd')) so the ends are not biased.
findings.risk: The bow deck line moves out up to about 11 mm at x=150-450, back to the traced line. Maximum beam grows from 2681 to about 2696 unless it is constrained (see curves-9).

findings.title: Sheer table DECK_EDGE_Z has an S-wiggle between 3000 and 4500
findings.claim: The measured sheer table is piecewise linear with non-monotonic slopes in the middle of the boat, so the sheer curvature changes sign 5 times. Two of those reach the loft as a short S at x of about 4130-4160.
findings.evidence:
params.py:117-123. Slopes 2500-5000: -0.050, -0.037, -0.016, -0.033, -0.020. Kinks: +0.72 deg (3000), +1.25 (3750), -1.02 (4200), +0.76 (4500). The 4200 point sits 3.2 mm above the 3750-4500 chord.

After _fair there are 4 sign changes. The exact loft deck edge has profile curvature sign changes at 2640, 4130, 4160 and 5870. The sheer itself is reproduced within 0.33 mm by the loft.
findings.fix: A cubic smoothing spline through the 18 points (scipy make_smoothing_spline, lam of about 4e7). Maximum residual is 5.0 mm (at x=2000, the corner the table puts there), against 7.1 mm for today's sheer_z. Inflections fall from 5 to 2 (2720, 5855).
findings.risk: Very low: 3-5 mm full scale is 0.1-0.17 model mm.

findings.title: WATERPLANE and SECTION_FULLNESS are piecewise linear, so the topsides are wavy at the stations
findings.claim: wl_half_breadth and fullness use np.interp through 14 and 9 control points. section() starts the topside curve at the DWL half-breadth, so every kink runs up the whole topside. The loft interpolates the 42 sampled sections, and its waterlines get curvature peaks at the stations and many inflections. This matches the wavy, faceted shading seen in the earlier flat-shaded renders.
findings.evidence:
curves.py:122-140 and 156-176.

wl_half_breadth kinks: 6.9, 5.3, 5.7, 5.4, 2.8, 3.8, 2.9, 1.9, 3.9 and 7.9 deg at x=1276-6703, and 26.9 deg at 7239 and 23.3 deg at 7708. SECTION_FULLNESS dm/dx jumps at 795, 1590, 2544, 3578 (-0.145/m), 4611 (-0.138/m), 5724 and 6758.

Exact B-rep waterlines, curvature sign changes between x=600 and 7400: z=+150: 18, z=+400: 17, z=+700: 11, z=+900: 5. The peaks sit 0-7 mm from stations; for z=+700 the peaks are at 790/995/1225/1980/6725/7155/7495 and the stations at 797/1000/1221/1987/6729/7153/7495.

Short-wave (<1 m) wiggle over x=1500-6800 is 3.98, 3.21, 1.93 and 1.04 mm full scale (up to 0.13 model mm). At the stern there is a wave: curvature about -1.8 1/m at 7150-7250 and +0.5 at 7495, caused by the 27 deg kink at 7239 (Image 1, bottom panel).
findings.fix: These are reconstruction parameters, not measured data. Replace _table's np.interp with a C2 spline through the same points: scipy CubicSpline with bc_type='natural' for WATERPLANE (or PchipInterpolator if overshoot appears near t=0), and the same for SECTION_FULLNESS. Spread the aft WATERPLANE points (0.85-1.015) so the narrowing into the transom does not hinge at 7239. Optionally add loft stations (for example 60) once the input is C2.
findings.risk: Displacement and section areas change slightly (the README already says not to use them for hydrostatics). Check that wl_half_breadth stays at or below the deck half-breadth.

findings.title: bottom_z steps 91 mm at the forefoot (x=1008), creasing every topside waterline at x of about 1000
findings.claim: Forward of LWL_FWD the stem formula takes bottom_z to 0 at 1008, but the faired table there is -91 mm. At the same x, section() switches from the stem branch to the underwater branch. The topside half-breadth slope therefore jumps at 1008, and the station at x=1000 samples it.
findings.evidence:
curves.py:114-119 and 155-166. bottom_z(1007)=+0.2 and bottom_z(1008)=-91.1.

Half-breadth at z=700: 220.6 (x=1000), 222.5 (1008), 229.1 (1020), 245.7 (1050). The slope goes from 0.24 to 0.55, a kink of about 15 deg about 0.7 m above the DWL. At z=150 the slope goes from 0.17 to 0.7.

The exact loft waterlines have curvature spikes at x=995-1003: +5.4 1/m (z=150), +2.65 (z=400), +1.65 (z=700), +1.0 (z=900). bottom_z also has kinks of 3.6, -6.5 and 17.8 deg at 7500, 7650 and 7800, but those are below the DWL near the transom.
findings.fix: Make bottom_z continuous: blend the stem curve into _ZB over about 150-300 mm (for example, start the stem formula from bottom_z of the table at LWL_FWD, or define the whole keel/stem profile as one spline through the traced uw_station.csv points). Also make the topside start point y0 continuous across the zb<-1 branch switch (blend bw between the 0.55*wl rule and the superellipse branch).
findings.risk: Touches the forefoot and stem profile, which is traced data. Keep the blend inside the drawing line width and recheck the bow void margins (VOID_BOW_EXTRA).

findings.title: Rubbing strake is a ruled loft: a polyline with uneven facets at 43 stations
findings.claim: The strake is ruled=True through rectangles at C.stations(48), so its edges are straight between stations in the CAD itself, not only in the STL. It follows the hull side at strake height, which carries the waviness from curves-5, so the facet angles are irregular. Of all the hull lines, the strake is the one the eye follows most.
findings.evidence:
hull.py:122 and 173 (ruled=True), 92-101 and 127-128 (yc from section()).

In the STL the strake's top-outer corner has vertices at the strake stations (1005, 1188, 1387, ... 7269; spacing 184-265 mm amidships). Plan turning at those vertices is 0.6-2.5 deg and uneven (for example 6550: -2.54, 6749: -0.76, 6935: -2.36, against about 1.4 deg for a fair line at that spacing). Profile turning is up to 0.66 deg.

strake_z itself has 7 curvature sign changes and the _fair end kinks (-0.70 deg at 150).
findings.fix: Build the strake from smooth inputs: fair strake_z (smoothing spline through the CSV column, tolerance 3 mm) and the side half-breadth yc(x) at strake height, then use makeLoft(ruled=False) or sweep a 95 x 110 profile along a 3D spline through the faired path. Combine with the absolute-tolerance export from curves-1.
findings.risk: A smooth loft through 48 twisted rectangles can self-intersect at the transom corner. Keep a ruled segment across the transom, or sweep with an auxiliary-spine or binormal mode.

findings.title: Deckhouse tables: COAMING_TOP_Z is wavy; COACH_TOP has two mild kinks
findings.claim: Both tables are interpolated linearly with deckhouse._interp and then lofted through 13 sections, so their kinks reach the solid. The coaming top changes curvature sign 3 times.
findings.evidence:
deckhouse.py:27-38, 41-43, 62-75 and 128-150 (13 sections, steps=12).

COACH_TOP (params.py:140): kinks -1.66 deg at 3000 and -0.88 deg at 4200, no inflection. The roof loft has about 335 mm spacing, so this is mild.

COAMING_TOP_Z (params.py:186-189): kinks -4.33 (5800), +0.56 (6000), +3.67 (6200), -1.70 (6400), +2.56 deg (6600). That is 3 sign changes, with local dips of 6.5 mm at 6200 and 4.5 mm at 6600 against the neighbouring chords (0.15-0.2 model mm). coaming_top_z adds two more slope breaks: max() against deck+40 and the linear blend between 6800 and 6900. The coaming loft spacing is about 153 mm, so the waves reach the solid.
findings.fix: Use a smoothing spline through COAMING_TOP_Z (residual 5 mm or less) and through COACH_TOP (or PCHIP). Replace the hard max() and the linear blend with a smooth blend (smoothstep over about 150 mm).
findings.risk: Low. The changes are a few mm and stay within the profile drawing's line width.

findings.title: Fairing proposal: splines through the measured points within one drawing line width
findings.claim: Replacing np.interp plus _fair with fairing splines removes every kink, the 7300 step and the bow S-bend. Each spline is fitted directly to the measured points and lies closer to them than today's curves.
findings.evidence:
Deck outline: least-squares cubic B-spline (scipy make_lsq_spline) through deck_halfbreadth.csv for x<7300 plus STERN_OUTLINE (weight 10). Interior knots: 800, 1600, 2400, 3200, 4000, 4800, 5600, 6400, 7000, 7400, 7600, 7700, 7760, 7800, 7830, 7860.
- Maximum residual: 10.9 mm on the trace outside 2450-3250 (today 11.6), 11.2 mm in the 2516-3220 dent-then-bump stretch of the trace (today 13.5), 3.1 mm on STERN_OUTLINE.
- The 1:50 drawing's 0.25 mm line width is 12.5 mm full scale, so all residuals are within one line width.
- Plan curvature sign changes between 300 and 7600: 3 (710, 1135, 7400), against 9 today.
- Maximum beam becomes 2696 instead of 2681. If the brochure 2680 is to stay, scale y by 0.994 or add a max-beam constraint.

Sheer: make_smoothing_spline through the 18 DECK_EDGE_Z points with lam of about 4e7. Maximum residual 5.0 mm (today 7.1); 2 inflections.

Proxy for what the loft makes of these (cubic interpolation through the 42 station samples): curvature sign changes fall from 6 to 4 for the deck and from 4 to 2 for the sheer. Before/after curvature plots are in Image 3.
findings.where: hr26/curves.py:42-106 (replace _load/_fair/np.interp for hb, zs, zk); params.py tables unchanged
findings.fix: In curves.py, build the splines once at import (scipy is available, or write a small numpy cubic B-spline) and evaluate them in deck_half_breadth, sheer_z and strake_z. Remove the 7300 switch and the _fair calls, and keep the hold section past the transom corner (_stern_table) as the continuation. Rebuild, rerun the overlays (overlegg-plan.jpg, overlegg-profil.jpg) to confirm the lines still sit on the drawing, and export with relative=False (curves-1).
findings.risk: Changes measured-line positions by up to about 12 mm full scale (0.4 model mm), toward the raw trace. The overlays and the beam check in the README need re-verifying. scipy becomes a build dependency unless the spline is written in numpy.
